packaged_recursive.oracle_note: Source-global labels use App.total; method identity retains sample.App.selected(int). Initial verification used the wrong global-root label; no application rerun was required.

checks: Complete independent receiver/static/outcome and alias/cycle oracles pass for every repeat, including the two deliberately different state cases.
Generated suites, per-case replay, detached export after original source removal, scalar shrinking from seven to zero and seven refusal controls pass.

Actual JVM PID/argv, 155 retained compiler manifests, 467 class bindings, all runtime archives and decoded protobuf batch/unit accounting are independently rechecked; copied original shrink evidence is not a new launch.
A separately packaged recursive method delivers two spans per instrumented repeat, exact nonempty stdout/stderr and independently expected complete typed state over four actual JVMs.
The frozen CLI retains legacy Java matching/mutation behaviour over eight additional JVMs.
Both 62-file SDK source copies and both pinned/prebuilt Java products remain unchanged; original short runtime directories are removed.
limits: Fixed JDK21 source-classpath diagnostic builds on macOS ARM64; external classpaths, modules, annotation processing, custom loaders and arbitrary flags remain unsupported.
Witnessing binds selected names, loaded classes, actual PID, policy and selection; invocation-scoped attribution and arbitrary concurrent activity remain open.
Direct health covers the supported SDK pipeline and independent local receipt; downstream collector processing, partial rejection and lifetime completeness are not inferred.
Live metric controls, broader object/sequence factories, shipping artefacts, other replacement-SDK language adapters and other platforms remain open.

The recursive receiver request-cap failure was fixed before this runtime commit. The supplementary verifier initially used a fully qualified global root label; its retained protocol uses global:App.total. The corrected literal oracle checks the existing four launches without rerunning them.
